memories.content: Conduct one review prior to submission focusing solely on the validity of user problems, design interventions, and evaluation logic.
Cross-check whether research questions align with the core functions of the prototype.
Cross-check whether evaluation tasks align with representative measures.
Cross-check whether collected evidence aligns with design and operational decisions to be changed.
Verify at the end that user problems, design interventions, user studies, and expected contributions form a coherent logical flow.
HCI reviewers view the validity of design interventions as low if research questions are not linked to prototype functions.
HCI reviewers view the validity of evaluation plans as low if evaluation tasks do not produce representative measures.
HCI reviewers view the practicality of contributions as low if collected evidence cannot change design or operational decisions.
Cross-check at the end whether each research question, formative evaluation data, and design modification judgment are seamlessly connected.
Review whether the application conditions of proposed design principles and boundary cases of failure are presented together.
The user can have contributions reviewed only if prototype outcomes and the transferable design knowledge derived from them are separated.
The scope of observation in controlled formative evaluations does not include long-term adaptation and operational changes in real-world usage contexts.
Do not change names referring to the same user roles, system functions, or operational stages midway.
Use abbreviations only for long recurring terms in a two-page proposal.
Present the full term and abbreviation together when using an abbreviation for the first time.
Refer to participants based on the roles they perform in the study rather than their status.
Reviewers from different subfields find it difficult to infer an abbreviation from context alone when it is not defined at first use.
When introducing an operational role for the first time, define both the decisions it can make and the actions it performs.
Individuals holding identical job titles may possess different system modification privileges and data access rights depending on their deployment site.
The user tends to group distinct field roles under the single label “user.”

analysis.overview: The frames address separate but complementary review concerns: the reference frame governs substantive HCI argument validity, evidence, contribution scope, and evaluation limits, while the compared frame governs terminology, abbreviations, and precise role descriptions. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame establishes this overall substantive review mandate.
relations.summary: A pre-submission review should focus specifically on the validity of user problems, design interventions, and evaluation logic.

relations.reason: The paired memories state the alignment check and its reviewer-facing rationale; the compared frame has no counterpart concerning research-question alignment.
relations.summary: Research questions should be linked to prototype functions so that design interventions appear valid to HCI reviewers.

relations.reason: The paired memories state the evaluation-measure check and its reviewer-facing rationale; the compared frame does not address measurement validity.
relations.summary: Evaluation tasks should yield representative measures so that the evaluation plan appears valid to HCI reviewers.

relations.reason: The paired memories express the same actionability requirement and its reviewer-facing consequence; no compared-side claim addresses evidentiary actionability.
relations.summary: Collected evidence should support changes to design or operational decisions so that claimed contributions remain practical.

relations.reason: Both memories specify final checks on connected proposal logic at complementary levels of detail, with no compared-side equivalent.
relations.summary: End-stage review should verify a coherent chain connecting problems, research questions, interventions, study evidence, modification judgments, and expected contributions.

relations.reason: This contribution-scope requirement appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Proposed design principles should present both their application conditions and their failure boundaries.

relations.reason: This distinction between artifact outcomes and transferable knowledge appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Prototype outcomes should be separated from the transferable design knowledge derived from them when presenting contributions for review.

relations.reason: This explicit limitation on evaluation scope appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Controlled formative evaluations do not observe long-term adaptation or operational change in real-world use contexts.

relations.reason: The compared frame alone establishes this cross-document naming-consistency policy.
relations.summary: Names for the same user roles, system functions, and operational stages should remain consistent throughout the proposal.

relations.reason: This format-specific restriction on abbreviation use appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: In a two-page proposal, abbreviations should be reserved for long terms that recur.

relations.reason: The paired memories provide the first-use rule and its cross-subfield readability rationale; the reference frame has no abbreviation policy.
relations.summary: An abbreviation should be introduced alongside its full term because reviewers cannot reliably infer undefined abbreviations from context.

relations.reason: The paired memories express a role-specific naming policy and the labeling problem it addresses; the reference frame has no counterpart.
relations.summary: Study participants should be named by their functional roles rather than status or the undifferentiated label “user.”

relations.reason: The paired memories state the role-definition requirement and the deployment variation motivating it; the reference frame does not define operational roles.
relations.summary: Operational roles should be defined by their decisions and actions because identical job titles can carry site-specific modification privileges and data-access rights.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers stable terminology, disciplined abbreviation use, first-use definitions, role-based participant naming, and operational-role descriptions that account for site-specific authority and access.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame covers pre-submission validation of problem–intervention–evaluation logic, actionable evidence, coherent research chains, transferable contribution claims, design-principle boundaries, and limits of controlled formative evaluation.
